Meanwhile Salesforce's parsing was switched to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`, which conditionally applies the credential-sharing minimum schema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set. So Salesforce is half-integrated into the new credential-sync feature: with sharing enabled, its parsing changes but its token refresh still always hits Salesforce directly, leaving accounts whose refresh token is held by the parent application unsupported. This is a real, diff-grounded incompleteness (an incomplete migration) rather than demonstrably incorrect behavior, so it warrants maintainer attention as an advisory.

Looking at the diff, other calendar services (Google, Office365, Lark, Zoho, etc.) wrap their refresh token fetch calls with `refreshOAuthTokens()` to support credential sync. However, in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` for parsing but does NOT wrap the fetch call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. The fetch at line 75 directly calls Salesforce's token endpoint without the wrapper. This is inconsistent with the pattern used in all other services and means Salesforce won't delegate to the credential-sync endpoint when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, even though it uses the shared response parser.
